subject: Synthesis: model scouting & parity decision items (Post-demo)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ava Thompson <ava@finbridge.com>, Samir Rao <samir@finbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Synthesis: model scouting & parity decision items (Post-demo)

Hi Ava / Samir — great demo catch-up earlier. Quick synthesis and suggested next steps so we can scope a short parity spike. I pulled the team notes and attached the prompt set + demo recording.

Key notes from demo:
- Primary workload: multi-turn customer support triage + ticket summarization (medium-long context, many short exchanges).
- Latency target: P95 <= 800ms for 512 tokens (customer-facing interactive UI).
- Cost sensitivity: target ~40–55% of current prop baseline cost for inference unit.
- Failure modes: hallucination around policy citations, occasional truncation on long tickets.

Initial model scouting (recommendations to test):
1) LlamaX-70B-QLoRA (open) — strong instruction following, good for long context with KV cache. Quantized variant to hit cost goals.
2) RedWood-Base-v2 (proprietary baseline) — matched to current internal baseline; better safety filters out of the box.
3) LlamaX-13B-finetuned (open) — cost-friendly candidate for cheap tier if quality acceptable.

Questions / asks for FinBridge:
- Can you confirm a representative prompt bundle or 3 canonical flows we should include? (I attached prompt_set_v1.csv — feel free to edit.)
- Are there any hard compliance constraints (data residency / redaction) we should account for during the spike?

Proposed next steps (timeline):
- FinBridge: confirm prompt bundle + two sample tickets (by Fri, 6/12).
- Redwood SE: run a 3-day parity spike testing LlamaX-70B-QLoRA + Redwood-Base-v2 against your sample prompts, collect metrics (latency, token-cost, ROUGE/Factuality heuristics).
- Sync: 30-min readout + decision next Monday (6/15).

Attachments: finbridge-demo-recording.mp4, prompt_set_v1.csv, benchmark_summary.xlsx (initial template).

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ava Thompson <ava@finbridge.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@finbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Synthesis: model scouting & parity decision items (Post-demo)

Thanks Stephanie — this looks helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Acceptance thresholds: our product team is mainly worried about two things — (a) summarization faithfulness (we measure via factuality sampling + spot checks) and (b) latency under burst load. Do you have a suggested numeric threshold for the parity spike (e.g., >95% pass on factuality spot-checks, latency P95 within 1.2x of baseline)?
2) Cost: our CFO asked whether Redwood can give an estimate for per-request cost at the P95 latency target before we run the spike. A ballpark range is fine.
3) Security: we need to confirm that sample tickets remain in our control. We can provide redacted examples, but want to avoid any persistent storage on third-party infra for the spike if possible.

We can send 6 canonical tickets + 12 short exchanges by Fri EOD. Samir will coordinate.

—Ava
Ava Thompson
Product Manager | FinBridge

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Thompson <ava@finbridge.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@finbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Synthesis: model scouting & parity decision items (Post-demo)

Ava — quick answers and concrete proposal from the SE side.

Suggested numeric thresholds for the parity spike (these are starting points we can adjust):
- Summarization factuality pass-rate (spot-check sampling): >= 92% for parity candidate to be considered acceptable; if Greenwood baseline is at 96% we target within 4 points.
- Overlap/Similarity (ROUGE-L) relative uplift: within -5% of baseline is acceptable at first pass.
- Latency: P95 <= 1.2x of your current baseline P95; we'd prefer <=1.0x but acknowledge quantized open models can sometimes be slightly slower for 70B at high concurrency without optimized kernels.
- Cost: we expect LlamaX-70B-QLoRA quantized path to reduce tokenized cost by ~40–60% vs the current prop baseline depending on batching; we will produce per-request cost estimates during the spike (we'll include a simple cost model in benchmark_summary.xlsx).

Security and sample handling:
- For the parity spike we can run within your VPC/private deployment (no persisted sample data stored in Redwood hosted systems). If you cannot run a private test, we can accept redacted samples and run them on dedicated ephemeral infra with logs purged after the run.

What we'll deliver after the 3-day spike:
- CSV with per-prompt outputs for both models + metadata (latency, token counts).
- Benchmarked metrics sheet (benchmark_summary.xlsx) with cost model and scoring.
- Short readout slides with example failure cases and recommended mitigations (prompt rewrite, tool calls, retrieval fallback).

Links: Parity spike workspace (internal): https://drive.google.com/finbridge/benchmark-summary
Please confirm the sample tickets and we'll schedule the run for Monday morning (6/15 PST) if that works.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Staff Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ava Thompson <ava@finbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samir Rao <samir@finbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Synthesis: model scouting & parity decision items (Post-demo)

Perfect — thanks for the fast turnaround, Ben and Ava. Confirming next-run plan and owner list: 

- FinBridge: share redacted/approved sample tickets + any specific edge-cases to highlight (owner: Samir) — due Fri 6/12 EOD.
- Redwood SE (Ben + Marissa): stand up parity spike in ephemeral/private infra, run LlamaX-70B-QLoRA quantized vs Redwood-Base-v2, produce benchmark CSV + cost model (run window: Mon 6/15 - Wed 6/17).
- Readout: 30-min decision session Thu 6/18 (Steph to schedule).

If sample tickets arrive earlier we can move the run up. Also note: we will include a short prompt-sensitivity check (3 variants per prompt) so we can quickly identify stability issues and where prompt engineering helps.

I'll send a calendar invite for the readout this afternoon.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

Stephanie Nguyen
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
